Where these two files came from, and why they are committed rather than fetched
===============================================================================

Until 2026-10-16 custom-style.css opened with

    @import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;600
                 &family=JetBrains+Mono:wght@400;500&display=swap');

which cost three things at once:

  1. A render-blocking request chain three deep. The browser had to fetch
     myst-theme.css, parse it, discover the @import, fetch Google's CSS, parse
     that, and only then discover the font files. An @import nested inside a
     stylesheet cannot be preloaded or parallelised; a <link> at least starts
     at depth one.
  2. A third party on every page view, with no preconnect, which is also a
     third party that sees every reader's IP address.
  3. A GDPR exposure in a book that devotes a chapter to the GDPR. LG Muenchen I,
     20 January 2022 (3 O 17493/20), awarded damages against a site operator for
     exactly this -- embedding Google Fonts from Google's servers without
     consent, because the IP address reaches Google. data-protection.md cites the
     noyb complaints and the 2022 Google Analytics findings; serving the pages
     that say so from fonts.googleapis.com was the one thing the chapter argues
     against.

Self-hosting fixes all three. The files are committed, not downloaded during the
build, so that a deploy does not depend on a third party being up and the bytes
cannot change underneath us.


The files
---------

inter-latin.woff2           48256 bytes
  sha256 3100e775e8616cd2611beecfa23a4263d7037586789b43f035236a2e6fbd4c62
  Inter v20, latin subset, variable weight axis 100-900.
  From https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/inter/v20/UcC73FwrK3iLTeHuS_nVMrMxCp50SjIa1ZL7.woff2
  Licence: SIL Open Font License 1.1 -- OFL-Inter.txt
  Copyright (c) 2016 The Inter Project Authors (https://github.com/rsms/inter)

jetbrains-mono-latin.woff2  31432 bytes
  sha256 83c005d49d8a6a50474c73a5a36ac0468076e9c4a29da7bdb14995d80560a5be
  JetBrains Mono v24, latin subset, variable weight axis 400-800.
  From https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/jetbrainsmono/v24/tDbv2o-flEEny0FZhsfKu5WU4zr3E_BX0PnT8RD8yKwBNntkaToggR7BYRbKPxDcwg.woff2
  Licence: SIL Open Font License 1.1 -- OFL-JetBrainsMono.txt
  Copyright 2020 The JetBrains Mono Project Authors (https://github.com/JetBrains/JetBrainsMono)

Both licences permit redistribution; both require the licence to travel with the
font, which is what the two OFL files next to this one are for. Neither font may
be sold on its own and neither is being sold.

These are the exact bytes Google served for the @import that was removed, fetched
with a current Chrome user agent so that the woff2 rather than the ttf variant
came back. Downloading them changed nothing about which glyphs a reader sees.


One file per family, not one per weight
---------------------------------------

The old @import asked for Inter 400 and 600 and JetBrains Mono 400 and 500. Google
answered both weights of each family with the *same* URL: these are variable fonts
and the latin subset carries the whole weight axis. So two files cover four weights,
and `font-weight: 400` and `600` are interpolated from one face. Asking for a third
weight later costs no extra request.


Coverage, and what deliberately falls back
------------------------------------------

The latin subset is U+0000-00FF plus the general-punctuation block, so it covers
every character the running text actually uses: the German umlauts and sharp s in
Voelkel, Duesseldorf and the glossary (ä ö ü ß Ö), the accented names (é), the
en dash in Kullback-Leibler, and curly quotes.

It does not cover Greek or the mathematical operators -- sigma, <=, and the rest.
That is not a regression: the subset Google served was the same one, so those
characters fell back to the system font before and fall back to it now. In the
mathematics proper they never did either way, because KaTeX ships and uses its
own fonts.


Updating them
-------------

Refetch both URLs, check the sha256 here against what arrives, and if it differs
read why before committing: a new vN in the path is a new release and worth a look
at the changelog, while the same path serving different bytes is worth more than
that. The CI guard in pages.yml checks that the files are present and that no
build reaches fonts.googleapis.com or fonts.gstatic.com again; it does not pin the
hashes, because a font that has legitimately been updated should not turn the
build red.
